measurements.mechanism_closure: (a) merge evidence: arrival-cluster shift above (the pre-registered syscall-count census was unmeasurable — sendto excluded — disclosed with the live probe proof); (b) arrival-cluster vs park-gap arithmetic at the measured round spreads: rounds gate the workload (p50 24-100ms per leg, 16-session append-completion variance; park 8ms between rounds), the collector writer parks BETWEEN rounds in BOTH binaries, and within a round the queue drains at arrival rate (most inter-frame gaps <=20us), so the writer's wake cadence is round-gated, not frame-gated; cand merges the occasional 2-5-frame cluster and saves only those few 15-40us park-wakes — ~100x below the shape's between-leg CPU/append spread (435-3533us); (c) the shape class where coalescing cannot help now has THREE measured members: continuous deep backlog (never parks), trickle with gaps > drain time (source lane), and ROUND-GATED bursts (park window between rounds; queue drains within the arrival spread) — the designed bursty shape lands in the third class. The precondition question is CLOSED: at the round-gated bursty shape the merge fraction exists at the wire but resolves no CPU; cand-c is dead at every io shape class tried (trickle, bursty-round-gated), and the next candidate on this surface would need a wake-cadence change (batch by park window, not by queue depth) or a shape with a continuously-backlogged writer — which is exactly the no-merge class.
